# AQK — Agent Quality Kit

> A standard and a CLI that check whether a repository is ready to have its code written by AI
> coding agents. Every rule the project promises to follow becomes a command with an exit code,
> so a machine holds the promise instead of somebody's attention. Reports a level from AQK-0 to
> AQK-3, computed by a run — never by a questionnaire and never by a model's opinion.

Vendor-neutral: works with any coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub
Copilot, Windsurf, Aider, OpenCode) and with no AI at all. It calls no vendor API and needs no
key. Stack-neutral: portable checks are plain `sh`; where the project already has a native tool
(ruff, eslint, knip, jscpd) the check uses it instead and says so when it falls back.

Zero runtime dependencies. Node 18+ and an `sh` shell. MIT.

## Use it

- Check an existing repository: `npx agent-quality-kit doctor` (read-only: writes nothing, sends
  nothing)
- Start a new one: `npx agent-quality-kit start`
- Install one guard from the catalogue: `npx agent-quality-kit add <name>`
- Check the minimum a project needs before agents can be handed the work:
  `npx agent-quality-kit doctor --baseline` (14 of 50 points confirmed by a run, ecosystem-neutral;
  the other 36 are named as a number, not hidden)
- Fail a pipeline below a level or on a failed gate: `npx agent-quality-kit doctor --run --min 1`
- Show only what a diff introduced, so a legacy repo is usable from day one: `doctor --run --since main`
- Prove the gates actually catch defects: `npx agent-quality-kit prove` — every *provable* gate is
  run against its own red and green sample and must go red on the first and stay quiet on the
  second. A gate with no samples, with samples written for another recipe, whose command takes
  no directory, or whose `requires:` program is not installed is reported as unprovable and
  named — never as broken; the verdict is "nothing proven is broken, and
  at least one gate is proven". Level AQK-2 and the badge depend on this, not on the presence of
  files
- See what proves a diff, file by file: `npx agent-quality-kit report --since main` — each changed
  code file is named by a check, walked past in silence, or touched by nothing at all, plus a
  fingerprint over the base, the commands and the file contents
- Put the repository state into the agent's context instead of hoping it reads the files:
  `npx agent-quality-kit context` — level, what is red right now, how many rules no machine
  enforces, what the ratchets hold. Where it does not know, it says so: a run that never happened
  is reported as unknown, never as clean. `context --install` writes a `SessionStart` hook into
  `.claude/settings.json` (Claude Code only; the rest of the kit stays vendor-neutral). Measured:
  the block is ~375 tokens, and carries what a file cannot — what changed today. `context --full`
  adds the command map and the rulebook verbatim (~7000 tokens): a deliberate trade, chosen by
  the owner after the objection about long inputs, on the grounds that an agent reads files
  poorly and the tokens are the price of it not guessing
- Check that the kit's own wiring is actually connected: `npx agent-quality-kit vitals` — are the
  tools the declared gates need installed, is the hook present in `.git/hooks` (a line in the
  config is an intention, not a guard), does the agent receive the state, is the version current.
  Four states, not two: connected · BROKEN · not connected and that is a choice · could not look.
  Only BROKEN affects the exit code
- See what your declared checks CANNOT see: `npx agent-quality-kit probe` — takes the files your
  own fix history calls hot, plants a proven red sample from the catalogue into a copy of each,
  and runs YOUR declared gates against it. Coverage is not declared, it is proven by planting.
  Three states that never merge: caught · nothing catches it · nothing to check with. Measured on
  the kit itself: a real file, a swallowed error and a debug print planted, 21 declared gates,
  none went red. The working tree is untouched and the exit code is always 0 — a look, not a
  threshold
- See what you told the agent and never wrote down: `npx agent-quality-kit learn` — reads Claude Code
  transcripts for this project on this machine and prints rule candidates missing from the entry
  point. Current project only, terminal only, writes nothing, always exits 0
- Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 below the level or a gate failed
- As a pre-commit hook: `repo: https://github.com/arsen-ask-lx/Agent_Quality_Kit` with
  `id: aqk` (blocking), `aqk-doctor` (read-only) or `aqk-baseline`. pre-commit installs the
  package itself; there are no dependencies to pull in.
- Without Node at all (a Python, Go or Rust project where nobody installed it):
  `docker run --rm -u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$PWD:/work" ghcr.io/arsen-ask-lx/aqk doctor`.
  Pushed to the registry by the same run, from the same tag, that publishes the package.
  Keep the `--user` flag: without it the container runs as root and
  the files `init` writes are owned by root, so you cannot edit your own manifest. Debian-based
  on purpose: the gates are `sh`, `grep`, `awk`, `find` — under alpine's busybox they behave
  differently, and an image where the gates behave differently is worse than no image
- As a GitHub Action: `uses: arsen-ask-lx/Agent_Quality_Kit@v0.9.0` with `min: 1`
  (https://github.com/marketplace/actions/agent-quality-kit-aqk)

## What makes it different

- The level is computed by running what the repository declares — not from a self-assessment
  questionnaire, not from the presence of a config file, not from a language model's judgement.
- Every guard must ship a red and a green sample, and a machine checks that the guard goes red on
  the red one and stays quiet on the green one. A check that cannot fail is indistinguishable
  from a check that works; this is the only place that requirement is enforced.
- An entry enters the catalogue only when it names a real failure it caught, recorded in the
  bruise journal.

## Files it reads and writes

- `AGENTS.md` — what the agent reads first (the entry point; `CLAUDE.md` and others work too)
- `.aqk.yml` — the manifest: entry, rules, docs, lang, gates as commands, covers (what a
  declared gate already holds, so it is not reported as debt), samples, ratchets, lessons
- `.aqkignore` — paths the scanning checks must not read (brought-in code, vendored, generated)
